transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Yes — a weak suction fault that has crept up over weeks is very often fixable, and emptying the bin alone will not cure a blocked filter or airway. I would not replace the vacuum yet. The leading possibilities are a clogged filter or a blockage in the hose/wand/floorhead; hair packed around the brush roll or a poorly seated seal are also possible. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Remove the washable filters, following the markings/manual. If they are dusty, rinse them in cold water only, with no detergent, then leave them somewhere warm and airy until completely dry — at least 24 hours. Do not refit damp filters. A restricted filter is a common cause of gradually worsening suction. 2. With the hose and wand detached, look through each section towards a light. Also inspect the bin inlet and the narrow neck above the floorhead. Remove any packed fluff, paper or debris you can safely reach; do not poke sharp objects into the hose. 3. Turn the floorhead over and remove any hair or thread wrapped around the brush roll. It should turn freely by hand. Check the bin and filter covers are fully clicked back into place as well. If it is still barely picking up crumbs after the filters are fully dry and the whole air path is clear, the next suspects are a split hose/seal leak or an internal obstruction/cyclone issue. At that point a repair assessment is sensible before buying a new machine; it is not yet enough evidence to condemn the motor.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Never washed the foam and felt filters before, didn't know they were there. The felt was caked with dust. Washed them in lukewarm water, dried them for 24 hours, and the suction is like new now. The hose and brushroll were fine, just a bit of fluff. No burning smell or overheating at any point.

That has fixed it: the caked felt filter was restricting the airflow, rather than a motor fault. There is no reason to replace the vacuum on this evidence. To prevent it returning, empty the bin regularly and wash the foam/felt filters periodically, then always allow them to dry completely before refitting. If suction drops again despite clean, dry filters, then check for a blockage or split hose/seal—but for now it sounds sorted.

candidates: Blockage in hose, wand, floorhead neck or bin inlet (high)
Hair-bound brush roll or air leak at hose/bin seal (medium)
